materiality: Past-recording sliding-window caches could return more KV columns than the advertised attention-mask width during multi-token assisted/speculative draft bursts.

Upstream documents eager mask/KV size failures and silent SDPA beyond-window attention divergence once sequences reach the sliding window, making this an output-correctness boundary rather than routine cache refactoring.
upstreamEvidenceBounds: Upstream reports a fail-before/pass-after layer regression, an end-to-end assisted-decoding parity fixture, a multi-token eager crash reproduction, five cache-cropping tests and 22 assisted-generation tests passing with three skips.
Those tests are upstream evidence only and do not qualify SZL model/assistant identities, attention backends, cache implementations, serving cancellation, concurrency or rollback.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact Transformers source/wheel/container plus exact target model, assistant model, tokenizer, generation configuration, attention backend and cache settings.

Add a deterministic known-bad predecessor fixture that proves recorded consecutive uncropped updates return over-wide KV while the candidate returns exactly the get_mask_sizes-advertised visible suffix.
Run fixed-seed greedy-versus-assisted output/logit parity after crossing the sliding-window boundary under eager and SDPA, including multi-token draft bursts and rejection/crop behavior.
Exercise cancellation, worker restart/cache reset, repeated requests and non-recording cache updates; prove the non-recording path remains unchanged.
Preserve rollback to the incumbent exact runtime and keep unexercised model/backend lanes UNQUALIFIED.

materiality: The xgrammar choice-to-EBNF path escaped quotes and backslashes but did not safely encode raw C0 control characters and DEL, so a requested literal choice could compile into a different grammar language or fail validation.
Structured choices can represent exact tool/action arguments; changing or rejecting their literal language is therefore a governed protocol-correctness boundary.
upstreamEvidenceBounds: Upstream adds coverage across every C0 codepoint plus DEL, multiline choices, quotes, backslashes and Unicode, including served validation conversion.
Upstream source tests do not qualify SZL's complete serving stack, xgrammar package identity, concurrency/error behavior or tool-authorization boundary.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact vLLM source/image/package and xgrammar package/build identities used in evaluation.
Use a deterministic independent literal-language oracle over C0/DEL, LF/CR/tab, quotes, backslashes, non-ASCII and multiline values; include the known-bad predecessor as a negative control.

Assert the exact intended literal is accepted while shortened, raw-escape and alternate-Unicode lookalikes are rejected, both through direct grammar construction and the actual served structured-output request path.
Exercise malformed/oversized choice input, validation failure, cancellation, concurrency and restart; no failure may silently fall back to unconstrained generation.
Preserve tool/human-approval authority independently of grammar validity and keep rollback to the incumbent exact serving path.

materiality: Deleting an active adapter can activate a fallback whose modules_to_save copy remains frozen, so the runtime reports an active training adapter while intended parameters do not receive gradients.
The same trainability re-synchronization gap existed for ShadowPEFT backbone/projection/head state; this is a training-integrity successor to the already-governed PEFT v0.21 boundary.
upstreamEvidenceBounds: Upstream adds focused modules_to_save and ShadowPEFT fallback trainability tests.
Focused upstream tests do not qualify SZL optimizer membership, checkpoint/save-load state, mixed adapter paths, exact package bytes or prior training receipts.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact PEFT source/wheel, PyTorch/Transformers stack, target model bytes and every adapter configuration exercised.
Use a known-bad predecessor and deterministic delete-active/fallback fixtures with and without modules_to_save plus ShadowPEFT; assert active-adapter identity and exact requires_grad sets.
Prove intended fallback parameters are present in optimizer parameter groups, receive nonzero expected gradients and change after one fixed-seed step while frozen parameters remain unchanged.
Exercise save/load/delete/switch/hotswap interactions and failure/rollback cases, and rerun relevant PEFT v0.21 state-dict/modules_to_save gates without inheriting their qualification.
Inventory any SZL training receipt that used active-adapter deletion/fallback on an affected source and mark it NEEDS_REVALIDATION if exposure is demonstrated rather than retroactively passing it.
